Header: 2026-03-04 14:00 UTC | Duration: 46 minutes | Attendees: Tom (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), James (CTO), Sara (ML Lead), Mark (Infra)

00:00 Tom Reyes: hey everyone, thanks for joining, should we do quick intros and then get into current infra? 
00:10 James Park: thanks Tom, i'm James, CTO at SilverPeak, Sara here is leading ML and Mark on infra, we're looking at dedicated GPU because of latency and data isolation requirements
00:20 Priya Nair: great, quick Q — are you running models in house now or calling hosted APIs? what models / sizes are you using?
00:30 Sara Kim: currently hybrid, some inference on prem for sensitive flows, we call hosted OpenAI for experiments, production is a mix — mostly 13B open weights and a few 70B for complex summarization. 
00:45 Mark Liu: infra is k8s on AWS, we have strict VPC peering rules and we need private networking, ideally no egress to public internet for PII workloads
01:10 Tom Reyes: got it, so sounds like dedicated or private fits. curious on traffic — what's your QPS and peak burst behavior?
01:22 Sara Kim: average 15 QPS for the 13B path, peaks up to 120 QPS during batch job windows, latency targets are P95 < 350ms for the 13B path, for 70B we're ok with 700-800ms
01:40 Priya Nair: ok that's helpful; with those numbers we usually recommend X GPUs reserved with autoscaling/burst headroom, we can do burst into pool capacity — do you need strict single-tenant isolation or is network/VPC isolation enough?
01:58 James Park: compliance wants tenant isolation for some flows, so dedicated nodes for those tenants would be ideal. other non-PII workloads could use shared hosting.
02:15 Mark Liu: and we need audit logs, KMS integration for key management, and SAML SSO for ops team — SOC2 is a must. 
02:30 Tom Reyes: we support customer-managed KMS/HSM, SAML SSO and audit logs — i'll share docs. Just to set expectations: Redwood Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools, configurable autoscaling, and burst policies to fall back to hosted capacity if you want that option.
02:55 Sara Kim: can you explain how burst works? would we be billed for burst separately? we want predictable monthly costs.
03:05 Priya Nair: burst is optional; you can reserve a base number of GPUs and allow burst for short windows. Billing can be structured: reserved commit plus short-term burst at higher rate, or cap burst to avoid surprise charges. we can model this in SOW.
03:30 James Park: performance question — how do you handle KV cache and long-context attention? our summarization uses 8k context windows.
03:45 Priya Nair: runtime supports KV cache management and attention kernels optimized per model; for 8k contexts we pick kernels and batching strategies to maintain low P95; sometimes we recommend quantization-safe variants for cost.
04:05 Sara Kim: any support for multi-model routing? we want automatic fallback from 70B to 13B for non-critical queries.
04:15 Tom Reyes: yes you can set routing policies by latency/cost/regulatory tags; automatic fallback to compatible model variants is supported. 
04:30 Mark Liu: network-wise, can we run the control plane in Redwood's hosted environment but keep inference in our VPC on dedicated hardware? 
04:40 Priya Nair: yes that's our Private offering pattern — control plane managed, inference private in VPC or on-prem; during pilots most customers run Dedicated with private peering.
04:58 James Park: timeline — we want a pilot in Q2, about 4 weeks to validate latency and isolation, then production by Q3 if all good.
05:12 Tom Reyes: perfect. For pilot success criteria, are we aligned: P95 latency targets met, security checklist completed, and cost per token within X% of your target? 
05:25 Sara Kim: yes those three. also include a small sample set of prompts and golden outputs for quality regression testing.
05:35 Priya Nair: we'll run a bench with your prompt set to measure tokens/sec, latency distribution, and cost curves — will also test canary rollouts/auto fallback.
05:50 James Park: one more — data retention: we need logs for 90 days, and no persistent retention of customer inputs by default.
06:05 Tom Reyes: default is no retention for user inputs unless enabled; audit logs can be exported to your S3 for retention, we'll include that in the security docs.
06:20 Mark Liu: curious about GPU types — do you use A100s, H100s, or maybe newer accelerators?  
06:30 Priya Nair: depends on region and availability; typical Dedicated pools use H100 for 70B and A100 for 13B, we can map to your performance/cost needs.
06:48 Sara Kim: any quantization recommendations? we saw degrade in some few-shot prompts previously.
07:00 Priya Nair: we do per-model quant profiles; for sensitive hallucination cases we tend to avoid aggressive quantization. we'll share suggested configs per model.
07:18 James Park: ok next steps?
07:25 Tom Reyes: i will send pricing and SOW for a 4-week pilot and options for burst billing; priya will attach security pack and a benchmark template; james/sara/mark to upload sample prompts and traffic profile. we'll target pilot kick-off week of 2026-03-16
07:50 Sara Kim: sounds good thanks everyone
07:55 James Park: thanks
08:00 Tom Reyes: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and i'll put calendar invite for kick-off once SOW reviewed
